Step–1  (Reaction with conc. H₂SO₄)  
•  Converting a vic-diol into a carbonyl compound in strong acid is the classical Pinacol–Pinacolone rearrangement.  
•  Therefore the substrate must be a vicinal diol.  
•  Among the options the only substrate that is a vic-diol is  
  2,7-dimethyloctahydronaphthalene-4a,8a-diol.  
  (The mono-ol proposed in options A & D cannot undergo a pinacol rearrangement.)

Step–2  (B + n-BuLi → acid work-up)  
•  Deprotonation of a benzyl (or allyl) ether with a strong base such as n-BuLi followed by protonation to give a homobenzylic (or homoallylic) alcohol is the [2,3]-Wittig rearrangement.  
•  For this rearrangement the starting material has to be an ether of the type R–O–CH₂–Ar.  
•  Only (((3-methylbut-2-en-1-yl)oxy)methyl)benzene fits this requirement and, after the [2,3]-Wittig rearrangement / protonation sequence, gives 4-methyl-1-phenylpent-3-en-1-ol.

Putting both parts together, the only choice that supplies the correct reactants for the two name reactions is option (C):

A = 2,7-dimethyloctahydronaphthalene-4a,8a-diol  
B = (((3-methylbut-2-en-1-yl)oxy)methyl)benzene

Answer: C
